ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The I-V characteristics of the zener diodes D1 and D2 are shown in the accompanying image, and these diodes are used in the circuit shown. If the supply voltage is varied from 0 to 100 V, which diode undergoes breakdown?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: Figure I shows the I–V characteristics of two zener diodes. The reverse-breakdown markings are near -80 V for D1 and near -70 V for D2. Figure II shows D1 and D2 connected in series on the right side of a circuit, with a variable 0–100 V supply on the left; from the diode symbols and the indicated supply polarity, D1 is placed in reverse bias while D2 is placed in forward bias. Reasoning: A zener diode undergoes breakdown only when it is reverse-biased and the reverse voltage reaches its breakdown voltage. As the supply is increased up to 100 V, D1 can receive enough reverse voltage to reach its approximately 80 V breakdown value. D2 is forward-biased in this circuit polarity, so it will conduct forward rather than undergo reverse breakdown, even though its zener breakdown voltage is about 70 V. Therefore breakdown occurs in D1 only.

Determine the bias from the diode symbols and source polarity: D1 is the reverse-biased diode, D2 is forward-biased. As the supply rises, the reverse voltage across D1 can reach its 80 V breakdown value because the maximum supply is 100 V. D2 cannot undergo breakdown because it is not reverse-biased under this polarity. Conclude: D1 only.

method.method_draft: Treat the circuit as an anti-series zener limiter. For the source polarity drawn in Figure II, the pair's conducting/breakdown state would be D1 in reverse zener mode and D2 in ordinary forward mode. The required supply for this state is approximately VZ(D1) plus the small forward drop of D2, about 80 V plus a small diode drop, which lies below 100 V. The alternative state, D2 in reverse breakdown, would require the opposite supply polarity, not merely a larger positive voltage in the shown direction. Therefore over the 0–100 V variation, only D1 undergoes breakdown.

推理：按图示电源极性，串联支路进入导通/限压状态时，D1 处于反向稳压击穿状态，而 D2 处于普通正向导通状态。因此需要的电源电压约为 D1 的稳压电压加上 D2 的正向压降，即约 80 V 加一个小的正向二极管压降，仍小于 100 V，所以 D1 会发生击穿。若要 D2 发生反向击穿，则需要 D2 被反向偏置，这对应相反的电源极性，而不是在图示极性下把电源从 0 V 增加到 100 V。因此在 0-100 V 的变化范围内，只有 D1 发生击穿。
